liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **The Other One** (2 reviews): Reviewer loves the sequence of The Other One into Me and My Uncle and back; Reviewer calls the Other One here incredible, and the sound fantastic [12][13]
- **Jack Straw** (1 review): Listener knew the albums but had never heard this song before the show [11]
- **Loser** (1 review): Jerry sounds very young on this one [14]
- **Tennessee Jed** (1 review): Reviewer was so impressed by this point that the show nearly made a personal top ten list [15]
- **Mexicali Blues** (1 review): Jerry's lead playing is described as cosmic [16]
- **Me and My Uncle** (1 review): Me and My Uncle fits well inside The Other One; the last note snaps the band back into the jam [14]

## Setlist highlights

- Earliest performances in the archive: You Win Again [18]

## The recordings

- **gd1971-11-14.sbd.lai.6254.sbefail.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 24 songs; 147 min; rated 4.5/5 by 2 [1]
- **gd71-11-14.weir.8738.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 24 songs; 147 min; rated 4/5 by 4 [2]. Said about its sound: Reviewer compared the two downloaded versions as wav files and found the other one clearly better in quality [12]
- **gd71-11-14.sbd.miller.23568.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 24 songs; 145 min; rated 3.93/5 by 27 [3]. Said about its sound: Reviewer rates the soundboard recording very good, about four stars out of five [6]
- **gd1971-11-14.170264.aud.lamarre.vernon.andrewF.flac2496**: audience recording; 16 songs; 87 min [4]. Said about its sound: Audience recording has several songs missing, with stand-alone songs cutting in and out abruptly and small fades [4]

## Around the show

- Reviewer attended TCU in the late 80s and was surprised the Dead had played the campus [6]
- Keith's piano energizes the band but he isn't fully integrated; Bobby carries most rhythm and Phil sings high harmonies [8]
- A Homecoming show at TCU; the crowd mixed blue tuxedos and gaudy gowns with hippies. First set ran sixteen songs [11]
- Pigpen is absent and Keith has just joined the band [17]
- Fall 1971 shows kept much primal energy but tempos were slowing, suiting blues and country ballads yet softening the psychedelic force [7]
- Show falls at a transition: Keith is in the band, Donna not yet; material mixes old songs with ones later on Europe 72 [8]
- Reviewer downloaded two versions of the show and found this one clearly better; sound is very good [14]
- Reviewer hears a feral energy usually associated with the 67-68 era, among the best of two decades of listening [17]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1971-11-14.sbd.lai.6254.sbefail.shnf**: transferred by Paul B and Mike Lai; source: SBD>MR>C>DAT>CDR [1]
- **gd71-11-14.weir.8738.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [2]. Also: Charles Weir produced a fix of the original soundboard source, including a written text file [2]
- **gd71-11-14.sbd.miller.23568.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [3]
- **gd1971-11-14.170264.aud.lamarre.vernon.andrewF.flac2496**: taped by Tape provided by Ann Saltmarsh to Doug Lamarre; transferred by Matt Vernon, Andrew F; source: Analog Audience Source: Unknown mic/deck/2nd generation AUD Source Taped By: Unknown [4]
